Pilots
pī´lŭts
n. pl. (steersmen; those who guided the ships of Tyre, and who mourn her fall)
Old French pilot, ultimately from Greek pedon, a rudder or oar-blade. The Hebrew of Ezekiel is chobel, from a root for a rope or cable — the man who handles the ship's tackling.

Biblical Definition

Ezekiel's lamentation for Tyre is built as a ship. “The inhabitants of Zidon and Arvad were thy mariners: thy wise men, O Tyrus, that were in thee, were thy pilots” (Eze 27:8). The wreck takes everyone: “thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise… shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin” (Eze 27:27). Then the survivors on shore: “The suburbs shall shake at the sound of the cry of thy pilots” (Eze 27:28), and “all that handle the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships, they shall stand upon the land” (Eze 27:29).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a pilot as one who steers a ship, and particularly one whose office is to steer a ship into or out of port, or in dangerous navigation.

expand to see more

PILOT, n. One whose office or occupation is to steer ships, particularly along a coast, or into and out of a harbor.

PILOT, v.t. To direct the course of a ship in a dangerous navigation.

MARINER, n. A seaman or sailor; one whose occupation is to assist in navigating ships.

Key Scripture

Eze 27:8 — "The inhabitants of Zidon and Arvad were thy mariners: thy wise men, O Tyrus, that were in thee, were thy pilots."

Eze 27:26 — "Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the east wind hath broken thee in the midst of the seas."

Eze 27:27 — "Thy riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise, thy mariners, and thy pilots, thy calkers, and the occupiers of thy merchandise, and all thy men of war, that are in thee, and in all thy company which is in the midst of thee, shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin."

Eze 27:29 — "And all that handle the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea, shall come down from their ships, they shall stand upon the land;"

Modern Corruption

Tyre's own rowers brought her into great waters, and the ruin came from the direction her strength was pointed.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 27:26 is the hinge of the lamentation and one of the most quotable lines in the prophets: Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters: the east wind hath broken thee in the midst of the seas. Tyre was not ruined by weakness. Her rowers were excellent, her pilots were her wise men, and they took her further out than anyone had gone — and that is where the east wind found her. The next chapter names the sin under the seamanship: thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches; thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas.

The corruption to name is competence without the fear of God, which Scripture treats not as neutral but as the accelerant of ruin. Tyre's judgment is not for incompetence and not for poverty; it is for a pride that grew directly out of genuine skill and real success. Ezekiel 28 traces the pattern behind it in language the church has long read as reaching past the prince of Tyre to the fall that stands behind every such fall. The doctrine for ordinary use is Proverbs' — pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall — and the picture for it is a first-rate crew rowing hard into open sea.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chobel (H2259), pilot, sailor who handles the ropes; mallach (H4419), mariner; qadim (H6921), the east wind.

expand to see more

Hebrew chobel (H2259) — pilot, shipmaster; Ezekiel 27:8, 27:27, Jonah 1:6.

Hebrew mallach (H4419) — mariner, sailor; Ezekiel 27:9, Jonah 1:5.

Hebrew qadim (H6921) — east wind; Ezekiel 27:26, Genesis 41:6.

Hebrew qinah (H7015) — lamentation, dirge; Ezekiel 27:2, 2 Samuel 1:17.

Hebrew gaboah (H1364) — high, lifted up, proud; Ezekiel 28:2, Proverbs 16:18.

Usage

"“Thy wise men, O Tyrus, that were in thee, were thy pilots.”"

"“Thy rowers have brought thee into great waters” — ruin by way of strength."

"“The suburbs shall shake at the sound of the cry of thy pilots.”"
